text: The Task's own merge logic was never the problem -- it simply stopped being scheduled. This lesson confirms exactly when, fixes it, and closes the monitoring gap for good.

TASK_HISTORY and QUERY_HISTORY pin the exact moment: a manual suspend during an unrelated warehouse maintenance change, five days earlier, never reversed. Resuming it and forcing an immediate run clears the backlog rather than waiting on the normal schedule.
The Stream drains from roughly four hundred thousand pending rows to zero, and the gold models reflect current sales again for the affected stores.
The real fix is structural: a new check added to the existing health monitor that alerts the instant any Task shows SUSPENDED -- closing the exact gap left open two lessons ago.
Proven by suspending the Task again and watching the alert fire within one cycle. Next: turning this incident into the story you actually tell Operations.
